problem:
Solve the inequality  ${x}^{2}\ge 100$ using a graphical method.

$x\in ($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$]⋃[$
{{field-3}}$,$
{{field-4}}$)$
worked_solution:
Bringing all the terms to the left-hand side, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & \ge 100 \\ {x}^{2}-100 & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the corresponding parabola given by $\,y={x}^{2}-100\,$ and find its roots:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-100 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-{10}^{2} & =0 \\ (x-10)(x+10) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So the roots are $x=\pm 10.$ 

Solving the inequality ${x}^{2}-100\ge 0$ is equivalent to finding the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y={x}^{2}-100$ is above or intersects the $x$-axis (where $y\ge 0$).

Since the leading coefficient of the quadratic expression is positive, the parabola opens upward. Therefore, the solution set lies outside the roots (including them), as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13965374/assets/6a6fe4b8f332bd821f27868586685f52d0dbcf326984ad683a27f41d5da473a4.png)

Therefore, the solution is 

$$
x\in (-\infty ,-10]\cup [10,\infty ).
$$
